correctness.rationale: For the stated Fourier sign, the divided-difference multiplier is (-i)^(-3)=-i; the constant-weight sum vanishes identically wherever the four phases are distinct. At the given reciprocal node, subtracting the constant exponential term leaves first real jet -sum w_j delta_j and quadratic imaginary jet (1/2)sum w_j delta_j^2. Denominator variation cannot contribute an imaginary quadratic term because the first exponential term becomes real. The real zero equation has nonzero gradient. On its tangent plane, elimination of v_3 gives determinant -w_0 w_1 w_2 w_3/w_3^2 for the quadratic matrix before the factor 1/2. The product of the four weights is positive because the six unordered pairs give six signs in the Vandermonde product. The restricted Hessian is therefore a saddle. The analytic Morse coordinates make its zero set precisely two axes on the real-zero surface: distinct tangent lines, and rank two off the crossing. At (1,2,3) the restricted quadratic factors as (v_2-v_1)(v_2-2v_1) after the common scale, giving the stated directions. The affine transport is invertible and multiplication by the nonzero translation factor preserves both zeros and the equation rank there.
residual_risks: Transverse here means distinct tangent lines within the common smooth surface. The theorem is local and real and requires all four scalar phases to be distinct. The finite moment and determinant tests are corroboration; the Hessian argument covers all nodes.

value.rationale: Complete reciprocal lattice nodes are naturally selected by exact phase cancellation, and their first Jacobian has insufficient rank to classify the zero set. The result distinguishes two crossing real branches from an isolated or higher-order singularity, gives their directions at every such node, and transfers to any affine tetrahedron. This is useful local geometry that a lattice census or transform evaluation does not recover.
residual_risks: No global component, repeated-phase, or higher-dimensional classification is asserted.
